question: When measuring the Marginal Reflex Distance-1 (MRD-1) to quantify ptosis, the examiner holds a pen torch at eye level and measures the distance from:

answers.text: The upper limbus to the lower limbus in primary gaze

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the vertical palpebral fissure height, not MRD-1. The palpebral fissure height includes the positions of both the upper AND lower lid, and does not isolate the contribution of levator dysfunction to lid position.

answers.text: The central corneal light reflex to the upper eyelid margin in primary gaze

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. MRD-1 = distance from the central corneal light reflex (pupillary reflex) to the upper eyelid margin in primary gaze. Normal MRD-1 is 4–5 mm. MRD-1 ≤ 2 mm indicates significant ptosis. It isolates upper lid position irrespective of the lower lid, making it the gold standard for quantifying ptosis severity.

answers.text: The upper eyelid margin to the upper limbus in primary gaze

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the limbus-to-lid margin distance, which is not the standard MRD-1 measurement. It is also affected by globe position (e.g. in proptosis) and cannot reliably quantify levator function.

answers.text: The central corneal light reflex to the lower eyelid margin in primary gaze

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes MRD-2, which quantifies the lower eyelid position. MRD-2 is relevant for lower lid retraction (e.g. thyroid eye disease) but does not measure ptosis. MRD-1 is always upper lid.

overallFeedback.feedback: MRD-1 = corneal light reflex to UPPER lid margin. This isolates the upper lid and is independent of the lower lid. Normal is 4–5 mm; ptosis is MRD-1 ≤ 2 mm. MRD-2 is the reflex to the LOWER lid margin, assessing lower lid position.

Correct. MRD-1 (normal 4–5 mm) from corneal reflex to upper lid margin is the standard ptosis measurement. Levator function is measured separately by the excursion of the upper lid from full downgaze to full upgaze (normal ≥ 15 mm).
